 368	// DisplayPath is how the UI and the prompt name one file, from a path given
 369	// either root-relative or absolute.
 370	//
 371	// Root-relative inside the project. Root-relative one level up too — a file
 372	// beside the project directory, or one inside a sibling of it — because
 373	// ../spec.md and ../sibling-repo/include/api.h say something an absolute path
 374	// does not: that the file sits next to the work. Absolute beyond that.
 375	//
 376	// The relative-inside, absolute-outside half is not a new rule; toProjectPaths
 377	// has written the resume file that way all along, on the grounds that a
 378	// reference reached outside the project has no project-relative form worth
 379	// keeping. The one-level exception is display's own, and storage deliberately
 380	// does not take it: a stored ../sibling breaks the moment the project moves,
 381	// while a name on screen only has to be right now. Two jobs, two rules, and the
 382	// divergence is in a file nobody reads.
 383	//
 384	// What it replaces named an out-of-tree pin by counting back to it, so
 385	// /usr/include/foo.h from a project three levels down read as
 386	// ../../../usr/include/foo.h — correct, and reading as though the file were
 387	// part of the project when the whole point of /read-only is that it is not.
 388	//

 390	// model call the file the same thing. That works because Workspace.contain
 391	// admits an absolute path for a pinned file, the same exemption unsafePath
 392	// makes — which it did not until this rule needed it.

 397	// displayName is DisplayPath for a caller that already holds a resolved
 398	// absolute path, skipping the re-resolve. Everything that names a pinned file
 399	// goes through one of the two.
 400	func (c *Coder) displayName(abs string) string {
 401		rel := c.relFname(abs)
 402		up, rest := 0, rel
 403		for {
 404			if rest == ".." {
 405				up++
 406				rest = ""
 407				break
 408			}
 409			if !strings.HasPrefix(rest, "../") {
 410				break
 411			}
 412			up++
 413			rest = rest[len("../"):]
 414		}
 415		// rest == "" is the project's parent directory itself, which is not a file
 416		// anyone pins; it falls through to the absolute form rather than being
 417		// named "..".
 418		if up == 0 || (up == 1 && rest != "") {
 419			return rel
 420		}
 421		// Native separators, not ToSlash. A root-relative name is the tool-facing
 422		// form — read, grep, and ls all report forward slashes, and it has to match
 423		// them. An absolute name is not in that world: it is a path outside the
 424		// project, which the user will read, copy, and paste somewhere else, so it
 425		// should look the way their OS spells one. CI caught the difference as
 426		// C:/Users/... where Windows means C:\Users\...
 427		return filepath.Clean(abs)
 428	}

 476	// confirmGrouped wraps c.Confirm with group-scoped auto-approve. If the user
 477	// answered "a" to a previous Confirm with the same Group, this one is approved
 478	// without prompting. The first "a" answer records the group and returns true.
 479	// req.GroupSession picks how long the record lasts — the session, or the turn.

 481	// c.Confirm.Confirm directly.
 482	//
 483	// Both maps are read on every call regardless of scope. A group is only ever
 484	// written to one of them, so this cannot widen a grant; what it does is keep a
 485	// session grant honored by a request that forgot to set GroupSession.
 486	func (c *Coder) confirmGrouped(req ConfirmRequest) bool {
 487		if req.Group != "" && (c.turnAutoApprove[req.Group] || c.sessionAutoApprove[req.Group]) {
 488			return true
 489		}
 490		res := c.Confirm.Confirm(req)
 491		if res.Always && req.Group != "" {
 492			if req.GroupSession {
 493				c.sessionAutoApprove[req.Group] = true
 494			} else {
 495				c.turnAutoApprove[req.Group] = true
 496			}
 497		}
 498		return res.Yes || res.Always
 499	}

 510	// runOne is the turn loop. It keeps sending while the model has something to
 511	// react to — a tool result it hasn't seen (OutcomeContinue) or a mistake to fix
 512	// (OutcomeReflect) — and stops when the model has nothing left to say, the
 513	// human interrupts, or a budget is spent. The turn boundary is still the
 514	// human's: nothing here starts new work of its own.
 515	func (c *Coder) runOne(ctx context.Context, userMessage string) {
 516		c.initBeforeMessage()
 517		c.turnHistory = ""
 518	
 519		if userMessage == "" {
 520			return
 521		}
 522		message := userMessage
 523	
 524		// Committing and rotating settled history are both turn-end concerns.
 525		// Mid-loop the tool results must stay in cur, and summarizing them away
 526		// between steps would compact the very results the next send reacts to;
 527		// committing mid-loop would spend one commit per send on fragments of one
 528		// change. A defer covers every exit — budget declined, reflection cap,
 529		// interrupted, or done. An interrupted turn's edits are real, so they are
 530		// committed too.
 531		defer func() {
 532			c.settleEdits("")
 533			c.endTurnHistory()
 534			// Last, so the accounting closes the turn: the commit line above it, and
 535			// nothing under it. This is what the per-send reorder was reaching for,
 536			// now at the scope where a reader actually wants the number. Once per
 537			// turn even when the turn was steered, because a steered turn is still
 538			// one turn's spend.
 539			c.flushTurnUsage()
 540		}()
 541	
 542		// Outcome-driven so a re-send that carries no message text — both a tool
 543		// reflection and a tool continuation re-enter on the appended tool results
 544		// — keeps the loop going.
 545		for {
 546			outcome, reflection := c.sendSteerable(ctx, message)
 547			// After the send, not during it: sendMessage does its interrupt
 548			// handling before returning, and that handling can retract messages.
 549			c.recordNewMessages()
 550			c.lastSendOutcome = outcome
 551	
 552			switch outcome {
 553			case OutcomeReflect:
 554				if c.numReflections >= c.MaxErrorReflections {
 555					c.Out.Warningf("Only %d reflections allowed, stopping.", c.MaxErrorReflections)
 556					return
 557				}
 558				c.numReflections++
 559				message = reflection
 560	
 561			case OutcomeContinue:
 562				c.numSteps++
 563				if c.numSteps >= c.MaxSteps && !c.confirmMoreSteps() {
 564					return
 565				}
 566				message = "" // the tool results are the message
 567	
 568			case OutcomeSuccess:
 569				// The model has nothing more to call, so it believes it is done.
 570				// That is the moment to check, if the project asked us to.
 571				report, ok := c.runAutoCheck(ctx)
 572				if !ok {
 573					return
 574				}
 575				message = report
 576	
 577			case OutcomeInterrupted:
 578				next, keepGoing := c.afterInterrupt()
 579				if !keepGoing {
 580					return
 581				}
 582				c.accumulateInterrupt(next)
 583				message = next
 584	
 585			case OutcomeLooping:
 586				next, keepGoing := c.afterLoop()
 587				if !keepGoing {
 588					return
 589				}
 590				c.accumulateInterrupt(next)
 591				message = next
 592	
 593			default:
 594				return
 595			}
 596		}
 597	}

 599	// accumulateInterrupt saves the content of a send that was stopped before the
 600	// next send resets it, so the transcript can show the full arc of a steered
 601	// turn: what the model was saying, the steer, and the final answer.
 602	//
 603	// The steer is included when the user typed a custom correction rather than
 604	// choosing "Continue" (which carries no user text). A blockquote prefix makes
 605	// the authorship unambiguous in the markdown transcript.
 606	func (c *Coder) accumulateInterrupt(steer string) {
 607		if c.partialResponseContent != "" {
 608			c.turnHistory += c.partialResponseContent + "\n\n"
 609		}
 610		if steer != "" {
 611			c.turnHistory += "> " + strings.ReplaceAll(steer, "\n", "\n> ") + "\n\n"
 612		}
 613	}

 615	// sendSteerable runs one send under a context of its own, so that stopping the
 616	// send does not have to mean ending the turn.
 617	//
 618	// This is the whole of the change that makes steering possible. Ctrl-C used to
 619	// cancel the *turn's* context: everything downstream saw Canceled from then on,
 620	// and there was no way back into the loop even though the conversation itself
 621	// had survived intact. A child context per send moves the blast radius to the
 622	// one send, and the turn context stays live to make the next one.
 623	//
 624	// The tool calls of a send run inside it too — applyToolCalls takes this same
 625	// context — so Ctrl-C still kills a bash command that is running, which is the
 626	// property worth not losing.
 627	func (c *Coder) sendSteerable(ctx context.Context, message string) (SendOutcome, string) {
 628		sctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 629		c.sendMu.Lock()
 630		c.cancelSend = cancel
 631		c.sendMu.Unlock()
 632	
 633		defer func() {
 634			c.sendMu.Lock()
 635			c.cancelSend = nil
 636			c.sendMu.Unlock()
 637			cancel()
 638		}()
 639	
 640		return c.sendMessage(sctx, message)
 641	}

 643	// InterruptSend stops the send in flight without ending the turn.
 644	//
 645	// Called from the REPL's signal handler, which used to cancel the turn context
 646	// directly. A Ctrl-C between sends finds no send to cancel and does nothing,
 647	// which is correct: there is nothing in flight, and the prompt the user is
 648	// about to get asked is the interrupt they wanted.
 649	func (c *Coder) InterruptSend() {
 650		c.sendMu.Lock()
 651		cancel := c.cancelSend
 652		c.sendMu.Unlock()
 653		if cancel != nil {
 654			cancel()
 655		}
 656	}

 658	// settleEdits commits the turn's edits so far and records a snapshot to undo
 659	// them by.
 660	//
 661	// Factored out of the turn-end defer because an interruption is also a place
 662	// this belongs. The human stopped to look at something, which makes that point
 663	// a review boundary: `git show` gives exactly what the model did before it was
 664	// stopped, separately from what it did after the correction, and /undo steps
 665	// through the two halves one at a time. Anyone who wanted one commit has
 666	// /squash.
 667	//
 668	// What is *not* here is flushTurnUsage. The spend is a property of the turn,
 669	// not of each leg of it, so it stays in the defer and reports once.
 670	func (c *Coder) settleEdits(message string) {
 671		// Nothing written since the last settle, so there is nothing to settle.
 672		// Without this an interrupted-then-steered turn settles twice over the same
 673		// edits: the second commit finds the tree already matching HEAD and
 674		// announces "the turn left the files as they were", which is true of the
 675		// second attempt and false of the turn.
 676		//
 677		// turnSnap is the right signal rather than turnEditedFiles, which
 678		// accumulates across the whole turn because the history record at turn end
 679		// wants every file the turn touched. turnSnap is emptied by
 680		// pushTurnSnapshot and rebuilt by recordWrites, so it means precisely
 681		// "written since the last settle".
 682		if c.turnSnap.empty() {
 683			return
 684		}
 685		c.commitTurn(message)
 686		c.pushTurnSnapshot()
 687	}

 689	// afterInterrupt asks the human what a stopped turn should do next, and
 690	// reports the message to resume with and whether to resume at all.
 691	//
 692	// The choice is put through the Asker port, which is what ask_user_question
 693	// already uses to prompt in the middle of a turn — so this is a shape the
 694	// terminal handling has been driving all along rather than a new one. Free text
 695	// comes back as the raw line, which *is* the correction, so there is nothing to
 696	// parse. A nil Asker means no interactive terminal (script mode): stopping is
 697	// the only honest answer there, and it is what an interrupt has always done.
 698	//
 699	// The --yes flags deliberately do not answer this. They skip permission
 700	// prompts, and being asked what you meant by stopping is not a permission
 701	// prompt — the same line the port's own documentation draws for
 702	// ask_user_question.
 703	func (c *Coder) afterInterrupt() (message string, keepGoing bool) {
 704		if c.Asker == nil {
 705			return "", false
 706		}
 707		// The edits so far belong to the interrupt, whichever way this goes.
 708		c.settleEdits("")
 709	
 710		answer := c.Asker.Ask(AskRequest{
 711			Question: "You stopped the model. What now?",
 712			Options: []AskOption{
 713				{Label: "Continue", Description: "Carry on from where it was cut off"},
 714				{Label: "Stop", Description: "End the turn here"},
 715			},
 716		})
 717		if len(answer) == 0 {
 718			return "", false
 719		}
 720		switch answer[0] {
 721		case "Continue":
 722			// Say what the user decided, or the model is answering the wrong
 723			// question.
 724			//
 725			// noteInterrupt runs before this prompt, so all it can say is that the
 726			// reply was cut off. On its own that reads as a full stop, and the
 727			// model obliges: "No problem — I'll stop here. What would you like me
 728			// to do next?" It is not misreading anything. Asked afterwards what it
 729			// had been told, it quoted the cut-off note and said no continue choice
 730			// had reached it, which was exactly right.
 731			//
 732			// The rest of the wording closes the other failure mode. With a whole
 733			// partial reply above it and no instruction about what to do with it, a
 734			// model will also quite reasonably begin again from the top — which is
 735			// what an earlier live pass showed, and what was wrongly written up as
 736			// the cost of keeping the partial rather than as this bug.
 737			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(

 89	// ParseGrants turns --yes values into the set AutoConfirmer reads. Each value

187	// ParseAskAnswer maps the line the user typed at a question prompt to the
188	// answer the model receives: the labels the indices select, or the raw input
189	// as one free-text answer. It is exported because two implementations of
190	// Asker need the identical rule — the REPL's terminal prompt and the fixture
191	// harness's scripted rows — and an answer interpreted differently between the
192	// two would make a replay lie about what a live session did.
193	//
194	// The rule, mirroring Claude Code's reference implementation: split on
195	// commas, and only if *every* token is a valid index in range do the indices
196	// select labels. Anything else — an out-of-range number, a multi-index
197	// answer to a single-select question, prose — is the whole raw input, never
198	// a partial interpretation, because silently dropping the tokens that didn't
199	// parse produces answers the user didn't intend.

202	// alone it is a custom answer the user left blank, so the answer is empty
203	// rather than the meaningless raw string "3".
204	func ParseAskAnswer(req AskRequest, input string) []string {
205		input = strings.TrimSpace(input)
206		if input == "" {
207			return nil
208		}
209		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(input); err == nil && n == len(req.Options)+1 {
210			return nil
211		}
212		tokens := strings.Split(input, ",")
213		labels := make([]string, 0, len(tokens))
214		for _, tok := range tokens {
215			i, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(tok))
216			if err != nil || i < 1 || i > len(req.Options) {
217				return []string{input}
218			}
219			labels = append(labels, req.Options[i-1].Label)
220		}
221		if !req.MultiSelect && len(labels) != 1 {
222			return []string{input}
223		}
